incidents.title: Single-region blast radius
incidents.brief: An availability-zone storm takes the only region offline and the product is unreachable worldwide.
incidents.constraint: RTO is 15 minutes; RPO is near-zero for orders.
incidents.question: What architecture reduces that blast radius?

choices.label: Second region
choices.resultBody: Run a second region with failover (or active-active) rather than one regional stack.

choices.label: Bigger VM
choices.resultBody: All users still depend on one region.

choices.label: More disks
choices.resultBody: More disks in the failed AZ only

hints: One region is the blast radius.

incidents.title: DNS failover too slow
incidents.brief: The primary region dies, but clients cache the old IP for 30 minutes.
incidents.constraint: TTL is 1800 seconds and there is no health-based routing.
incidents.question: What makes regional failover actually work?

choices.label: Second region
choices.resultBody: Health-checked global routing with short TTLs or Anycast, not static DNS alone.

choices.label: Hope users flush
choices.resultBody: All users still depend on one region.

choices.label: Keep 1-hour TTL
choices.resultBody: Keep a 1-hour TTL for easier caching

hints: One region is the blast radius.

incidents.title: Active-passive database lag
incidents.brief: Failover to the secondary region loses 12 minutes of orders because replication was asynchronous and unmonitored.
incidents.question: What must you design and measure?

choices.label: Read replicas
choices.resultBody: Replication lag SLOs, and a failover policy that matches acceptable data loss.

choices.label: Failover checking lag
choices.resultBody: All users still depend on one region.

choices.label: Synchronous cross-region commits
choices.resultBody: Synchronous cross-region commits for every analytics event

hints: One region is the blast radius.

incidents.title: Users pinned to a distant region
incidents.brief: APAC users always hit US-East even though an APAC stack exists.
incidents.question: How should traffic be steered?

choices.label: Second region
choices.resultBody: Route users to the nearest healthy region, with failover if that region is down.

choices.label: One global origin
choices.resultBody: All users still depend on one region.

choices.label: Manual country files
choices.resultBody: Manual country files on each laptop

hints: One region is the blast radius.

incidents.title: Config deployed to one region
incidents.brief: A feature flag is on in EU and off in US, so checkout rules disagree.
incidents.constraint: Flags must be consistent for a given user.
incidents.question: What multi-region concern is this?

choices.label: Read replicas
choices.resultBody: Replicate control-plane config with a defined consistency model, or pin a user to one region’s flags.

choices.label: Independent flags no

choices.label: Change flags region
choices.resultBody: Change flags only in the region that happens to be awake

incidents.title: Stateful sessions in one region
incidents.brief: Sessions live in regional memory, so a failover logs everyone out.
incidents.constraint: Users must survive a region loss.
incidents.question: Where should session state live?

choices.label: Read replicas
choices.resultBody: Replicated or globally reachable session storage, not process memory in one region.

choices.label: Sticky sessions single
choices.resultBody: All users still depend on one region.

choices.label: No session store
choices.resultBody: No session store

incidents.title: Split-brain writes
incidents.brief: Both regions accept order writes during a partition and two inventories diverge.
incidents.question: What write policy avoids split brain?

choices.label: Reshard data
choices.resultBody: A single-writer region or consensus so only one side accepts conflicting writes during a partition.

choices.label: Active-active writes no
choices.resultBody: All users still depend on one region.

choices.label: Last timestamp wins
choices.resultBody: Last timestamp wins on money

incidents.question: What readiness level is required?

choices.label: Second region
choices.resultBody: A warm or hot standby with scaled-out instances already running, not a cold start.

choices.resultBody: Keep regulated data and its serving path in-region; do not replicate restricted fields globally.

choices.resultBody: Elect a single region (or a lock) for globally unique jobs; run regional jobs only on regional data.

incidents.title: Follow-the-sun on-call vs follow-the-traffic
incidents.brief: Traffic is global 24/7 but only one region is staffed, so overnight incidents wait.

incidents.question: What must match the architecture?

choices.resultBody: No paging outside HQ

incidents.title: Global secondary indexes lag
